text:
lina.design: Hey team — quick sync on the Usage page mock. Posting two screenshots + a short list of open q's. main ask: which default view should surface for orgs with >1 project? :thinking:

lina.design: Screenshot A shows a compact spend card grid (cards per project) with inline token breakdown sparkline. Screenshot B is a single ledger table with an expandable project detail row. Thinking: cards = faster at-a-glance, table = scannable lines for finance folks.

matt.pm: my vote: default to cards for PLG-first users, but add a persistent "Switch to ledger" button top-right. Keep it discoverable. :+1:

jon.frontend: technically cards let us lazy-load charts which helps perf. Table needs server-side pagination for 100+ projects. doable but more work.

aisha.research: research note: power users asked for keyboard-first nav between rows in table. Cards were preferred by new users. We should support both accesibility-wise.

lina.design: good notes. A few micro UX nits: 1) token breakdown tooltip copy should be explicit about what counts as "billable tokens" 2) invoice download CTA positioning — should it live on the right of header or inside billing tab? 3) color contrast on the sparkline when in compact mode (fails AA on low-contrast themes).

jon.frontend: for tooltip copy, propose: `Billable tokens = tokens consumed by generation + model overhead (system tokens). Excludes embeddings and cached tokens.` simple and scannable.

matt.pm: +1 to Jon's copy. Also add a small link to billing docs: /docs/billing/token-metrics so finance teams can deep-dive.

lina.design: layout ask: if we keep cards default, I'd like legend ordering to match ledger row order (total descending). Right now mock sorts legend alphabetically which confuses users.

aria-ux-bot: quick accessibility check: contrast ratio for sparkline color #6b7280 on bg #ffffff -> 3.8:1 (below 4.5:1). Recommend #4b5563 or bold the line. Also ensure SVG has focusable elements and aria-labels for screen readers.

jon.frontend: noted. I'll change sparkline color to #374151 and add `role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Spend sparkline for project X\"` and keyboard focus on hover/focus.

aisha.research: invoice CTA: users expect an inline download button next to the invoice name (per interviews). Secondary place: top-right header for bulk downloads. So do both.

matt.pm: decision proposal: 1) Default view = cards for orgs with <20 projects, fallback to table for >=20 with prompt to switch. 2) Legend ordering: sort by spend desc. 3) Tooltip copy = Jon's text + link to docs. 4) Invoice CTA: inline per-row + header bulk action. 5) Accessibility: use #374151 sparkline, ensure aria labels and keyboard nav.

lina.design: love this. Two tiny copy tweaks: change "Billable tokens" -> "Billable token usage" and change tooltip sentence to end with "...Excludes embeddings and cached tokens." (with period).

jon.frontend: will implement copy as: `Billable token usage = tokens consumed by generation + model overhead (system tokens). Excludes embeddings and cached tokens.` and push a small CSS fix for focus outlines.

matt.pm: timeline? can we ship the copy + tooltip + color+ legend change next sprint, table fallback in the following?

jon.frontend: yup — copy + tooltip + color + legend ordering = 1 sprint. Table fallback (server pagination + keyboard nav) = 2 sprints.

lina.design: I'll update mocks and create a tiny acceptance checklist: 1) cards default under 20 2) switch persists in local storage 3) legend sort option 4) tooltip text & doc link 5) sparkline contrast + aria 6) per-row invoice download + bulk header. Posting updated figma link in a sec. :link:

aria-ux-bot: accessibility reminder: also test with high-contrast mode and screen reader NVDA/VoiceOver.

matt.pm: thanks all. If no objections I'll mark this design review as approved for scoped implementation next sprint. :thumbsup:

lina.design: approved from design. I'll follow up with final assets and copy strings. :party:
